verdict.rationale: Penpot documents token-authenticated programmatic access to its backend RPC API, described by an auto-generated OpenAPI spec, and promotes workflow automation and external rendering. It can also be deployed with docker compose or Kubernetes, so non-interactive, scripted use is supported. There is no documented headless runner, CLI, or CI integration guide, so running Penpot in CI pipelines is only implied by API access and containerized deployment. Missing for 10: an official headless/CLI mode, CI-specific documentation or examples, a documented headless export/render workflow, and hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Use access tokens as an alternative login authentication. They can allow an app to access Penpot's API.
Penpot's hosted SaaS instance serves a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0.0 document for the backend RPC API
Get extensive access to objects and properties to enable external rendering, workflow automation, enhanced app functionality, and more.
